heading: A costed fleet, not a promise
lede: Every hull in the forge is priced from the geometry that was actually drawn: cubic metres of oak, metres of seam to caulk, square metres of cloth, kilos of ironwork, and shipwright hours. Change a strake count and the timber volume changes, so the price changes, because there is more boat.

grid.p: Arithmetic on a costing. It is a ratio between two numbers on this page, not a price, not a valuation, and not a forecast.
Oak $/m³, shipwright $/hr, canvas $/m², yard overhead %. Move any of them and every figure above moves. They are defaults to argue with.

text: The fleet of ten hulls, costed from real geometry, and the ratio that falls out of dividing that cost by the supply.
